title: Augmentation-preserving shuffle isomorphism for bicosimplicial cochain totalizations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and use its ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\Delta$ be the category of finite nonempty ordered sets $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and order-preserving maps. Let $X:\Delta	imes\Delta	o\operatorname{Ch}^{\geq0}(\mathcal C)$ be a bicosimplicial object in nonnegative cochain complexes. Write $X^{a,b,r}$ for its terms, $d_r$ for its internal differential, and $\delta_1,\delta_2$ for the alternating coface sums in the two cosimplicial directions. All total complexes below have finite sums in each degree, as in [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Define
$$D(X)^m= igoplus_{n+r=m}X^{n,n,r},\qquad d_D=\delta_{\mathrm{diag}}+(-1)^n d_r,$$
where $\delta_{\mathrm{diag}}$ applies each coface in both directions, and
$$T(X)^m= igoplus_{a+b+r=m}X^{a,b,r},\qquad d_T=\delta_1+(-1)^a\delta_2+(-1)^{a+b}d_r.$$
For $a+b=n$, partition $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ into increasing lists $\mu$ of length $a$ and $
u$ of length $b$. Define order-preserving surjections $\alpha_\mu:[n]	o[a]$ and $\alpha_
u:[n]	o[b]$ by $\alpha_\mu(i)=\#\{j\in\mu:j<i\}$ and the corresponding formula for $
u$. Let $\epsilon(\mu,
u)$ be the sign of the permutation whose list is the concatenation $(\mu,
u)$. On $X^{n,n,r}$ define the component into $X^{a,b,r}$ by
$$S_{a,b}=\sum_{\mu\sqcup
u=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}\epsilon(\mu,
u)X(\alpha_\mu,\alpha_
u).$$
These components define a natural cochain map $S:D(X)	o T(X)$ which is a chain homotopy equivalence. In particular $S$ specifies a natural isomorphism $D(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(X)$ in $D(\mathcal C)$, not just isomorphisms of individual cohomology objects. If $M$ is a nonnegative complex and $i:M	o X^{0,0, ullet}$ is a chain map with $\delta_1i=\delta_2i=0$, it gives chain maps $j_D:M	o D(X)$ and $j_T:M	o T(X)$ supported in cosimplicial degree zero, and $S j_D=j_T$. This includes constant bicosimplicial objects, vanishing objects, and either cosimplicial direction constant.

proof.text: In $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta\times\Delta,\mathrm{Ab})$, take $P_n=R_{(n,n)}$ and $Q_n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}R_{(a,b)}$ with the boundaries and augmentations of [lem-sfb-free-bisimplex-projective-resolutions]. That lemma supplies projective resolutions, including repeated vertices. Apply [lem-sfb-universal-shuffle-homotopy-inverse] to these very complexes: it supplies the prescribed $\sigma:Q\to P$, its augmented inverse $\tau$, and both homotopies in the functor category.

proof.text: Evaluate the fixed universal equivalence with [lem-sfb-universal-shuffle-evaluation], obtaining homotopy equivalences whose forward maps have the required finite-subset formula. Naturality follows directly on each diagonal coproduct inclusion: move the diagram map through each shuffle arrow using its naturality square and through the target inclusion using functoriality of totalization; finite sums preserve these equations.

proof.text: Passing to the homotopy category, the two homotopy equations say that the classes of $S$ and its evaluated inverse compose to the identity. Their images under the localization defining $D(\mathcal C)$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] still satisfy these two equations, hence give an isomorphism of derived objects. The original maps commute with every map of bicosimplicial complexes by the finite matrix formulas, so this derived isomorphism is natural.

source.place: Paragraph (3), formal bicosimplicial homological algebra for the diagonal versus successive bar augmentations; universal free-simplex proof written by the worker.

proof.text: Write $f_0,f_1$ and $g_0,g_1$ for the degree-zero cofaces in the two directions. Their commutation gives $(f_0g_0-f_1g_1)i=g_0(f_0-f_1)i+f_1(g_0-g_1)i=0$. The separate coface sums also kill $i$. Together with $d_ri=i d_M$, these equations show that the degree-zero inclusions define chain maps $j_D,j_T$. The sole shuffle for $n=0$ has empty lists, sign $1$, and identity surjections, so $S_{0,0}=1$ and $Sj_D=j_T$ strictly. Zero diagrams give zero matrices. Repeated vertices were retained throughout, and no step assumes either direction nonconstant; hence both constant-direction cases and constant diagrams are included.

lean.statement: theorem exists_shuffle [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C] : ∃ S : ∀ X : SimplexCategory × SimplexCategory ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ, diagonalTotal X ⟶ successiveTotal X, (∀ (X : SimplexCategory × SimplexCategory ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ) (n r m : ℕ) (h : n + r = m), diagonalInclusion X n r m h ≫ (S X).f m = ∑ μ : Finset (Fin n), shuffleTerm X n r m h μ) ∧ (∀ (X Y : SimplexCategory × SimplexCategory ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y), diagonalMap f ≫ S Y = S X ≫ successiveMap f) ∧ (∀ X : SimplexCategory × SimplexCategory ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ, ∃ e : HomotopyEquiv (diagonalTotal X) (successiveTotal X), e.hom = S X) ∧ (∃ e : ∀ X : SimplexCategory × SimplexCategory ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ, (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((diagonalTotal X).extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)) ≅ (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((successiveTotal X).extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)), (∀ X : SimplexCategory × SimplexCategory ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ, (e X).hom = DerivedCategory.Q.map ((ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat.extendFunctor C).map (S X))) ∧ (∀ (X Y : SimplexCategory × SimplexCategory ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y), DerivedCategory.Q.map ((ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat.extendFunctor C).map (diagonalMap f)) ≫ (e Y).hom = (e X).hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map ((ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat.extendFunctor C).map (successiveMap f)))) ∧ (∀ (X : SimplexCategory × SimplexCategory ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ) (M : CochainComplex C ℕ) (i : M ⟶ X.obj (⦋0⦌, ⦋0⦌)), i ≫ (X.map ((SimplexCategory.δ (0 : Fin 2), 𝟙 ⦋0⦌) : (⦋0⦌, ⦋0⦌) ⟶ (⦋1⦌, ⦋0⦌)) - X.map ((SimplexCategory.δ (1 : Fin 2), 𝟙 ⦋0⦌) : (⦋0⦌, ⦋0⦌) ⟶ (⦋1⦌, ⦋0⦌))) = 0 → i ≫ (X.map ((𝟙 ⦋0⦌, SimplexCategory.δ (0 : Fin 2)) : (⦋0⦌, ⦋0⦌) ⟶ (⦋0⦌, ⦋1⦌)) - X.map ((𝟙 ⦋0⦌, SimplexCategory.δ (1 : Fin 2)) : (⦋0⦌, ⦋0⦌) ⟶ (⦋0⦌, ⦋1⦌))) = 0 → ∃ (jD : M ⟶ diagonalTotal X) (jT : M ⟶ successiveTotal X), (∀ m : ℕ, jD.f m = i.f m ≫ diagonalInclusion X 0 m m (Nat.zero_add m)) ∧ (∀ m : ℕ, jT.f m = i.f m ≫ successiveInclusion X 0 0 m m (Nat.zero_add m)) ∧ jD ≫ S X = jT)
